guide.title: History Taking (SAMPLE / OPQRST)
guide.lead: Most diagnoses come from the history. Ask open questions first and listen. Use SAMPLE and OPQRST so nothing is missed, check with family and the scene, and always ask about blood thinners.

sections.title: SAMPLE
rows: What's wrong? What do you see?
Including blood thinners, insulin, inhalers, recent changes

sections.title: OPQRST (pain and other symptoms)
rows: What makes it worse or better?
How long? Constant or coming and going?

groups.title: Technique
items: Open questions first, then closed ones to clarify
Ask family, carers, medication lists; look at the scene

groups.title: Red-flag answers
items: Chest pain over 20 minutes or not settling with rest or nitroglycerin: ACS
Black stools, blood thinners, new confusion

groups.title: Refusals: check capacity
items: Understands, appreciates, reasons, communicates a choice
Confusion, intoxication or head injury can remove capacity

quiz.q: A trauma patient on warfarin is at risk of:
quiz.explanation: Ask about blood thinners in every trauma.

quiz.q: Chest pressure for 3 hours, partial relief with nitroglycerin. Most concerning element?
options: The duration: suggests an evolving MI
quiz.explanation: More than 20 minutes suggests ACS rather than stable angina.

quiz.q: Sudden tearing back pain to the groin, pale, HR 122, BP 84/56 in an older man:

options: Signs/symptoms, Allergies, Medications, Past history, Last intake, Events
Symptoms, Age, Mechanism, Pain, Location, Events
Signs, Airway, Medications, Pulse, Lungs, Exam
Safety, Allergies, Mental status, Pupils, Lungs, ECG

quiz.q: The Q in OPQRST asks about:
options: Quality: what the pain feels like

quiz.q: Best first question for a conscious patient:
"Tearing" chest pain to the back suggests:
A patient wants to refuse care. Which suggests they lack capacity?
options: They can't explain the risks you described
They want to see their own doctor

quiz.q: Who often has ACS without typical chest pain?
options: Women, older adults and people with diabetes

flashcards.question: SAMPLE
flashcards.answer: Signs and symptoms, Allergies, Medications, Past history, Last oral intake, Events.

flashcards.question: OPQRST
flashcards.answer: Onset, Provocation/Palliation, Quality, Region/Radiation, Severity, Time.

flashcards.question: Why ask about anticoagulants in trauma?
flashcards.answer: Warfarin, apixaban, rivaroxaban and dabigatran raise the risk of life-threatening bleeding, even from minor injuries.

flashcards.question: Pain scale for pre-verbal or cognitively impaired patients
flashcards.answer: FLACC: face, legs, activity, cry, consolability.

flashcards.question: A patient refuses care
flashcards.answer: Check capacity, explain the risks, offer alternatives, involve medical direction if needed, document thoroughly, invite them to call back.

flashcards.question: Open vs closed questions
flashcards.answer: Open ("Tell me what happened") gives the story; closed ("Did it start suddenly?") clarifies details.

flashcards.question: Who has atypical ACS?
flashcards.answer: People with diabetes, women and older adults: fatigue, nausea, breathlessness, weakness or confusion.

critical.scenario: A 58-year-old with diabetes feels weak and tired. He plays it down. His wife tells you privately he had black, tarry stools yesterday and today. HR 108, BP 96/60, pale and cool.
critical.question: Which history changes the picture, and next action?

options.t: The wife's report of melena: upper GI bleed with early shock – lie flat, oxygen to target, IV access en route, rapid transport

options.f: Check glucose, but melena explains the picture.

options.t: Respect his wish not to discuss it and leave

critical.explanation: Always seek collateral history; patients often minimise.

critical.scenario: An injured driver with a deformed femur shouts that your questions are stupid and demands you drive now.
critical.question: How do you get the essential history?

options.t: Acknowledge his pain, explain briefly why you need allergies and medicines for safe pain relief, ask just those now, the rest en route
Insist on the full SAMPLE before moving

options.f: Allergies and medicines are needed for safe treatment.

critical.explanation: Trust builds once pain is treated.

critical.scenario: A 78-year-old living alone "fell", can't remember how, doesn't know the day, and wants only help up. Empty fridge; an empty bottle of her BP medicine.
critical.question: Best approach?

options.t: Treat the confusion as a possible cause of the fall; gather clues from the scene; she lacks capacity to refuse – explain kindly and transport
Help her up and get a signed refusal
options.f: She can't reliably understand the risks.

options.t: Call a taxi to her doctor
Force her onto the stretcher without explanation

critical.explanation: Ask about the events before the fall: infection, dehydration, missed medicines.
